claims.text: The as-cast Al0.2Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Ni0.2 alloy has a coarse grain size of approximately 98 μm.
The as-cast Al0.2Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Ni0.2 alloy contains BCC/B2 phases.
Stationary Friction Processing can refine this alloy to grain sizes of approximately 1 μm or 0.43 μm.
A processing-temperature range of 400–1800°C is suitable or relevant for the proposed SFP treatment, depending on strain rate.
Severe surface deformation produces an ultrafine-grained microstructure with high grain-boundary density and improved elemental homogeneity.
High grain-boundary density accelerates Al and Cr diffusion to the alloy surface.
Accelerated Al and Cr diffusion promotes rapid formation of a continuous, dense, adherent Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale.
The Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale limits oxygen ingress and ion diffusion and thereby reduces oxidation kinetics.
Grain refinement impedes dislocation motion and increases hardness.
Compositional homogeneity maintains the alloy's aqueous corrosion resistance.
SFP-treated Al0.2Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Ni0.2 will attain a Vickers hardness above 600 HV.
At 1000°C, the treated alloy will show more than 50% lower oxidation mass gain than the as-cast alloy.
The treated alloy will retain corrosion resistance in H2SO4 solution.
The as-cast alloy has a baseline hardness of approximately 300–400 HV.
Processing above 1400°C may cause Laves-phase precipitation and grain growth that degrade properties.
Oxidation testing at 900–1100°C is an appropriate evaluation range for high-temperature oxidation behavior.
The optimal SFP temperature and strain rate for balancing hardness and oxidation resistance are uncertain.
If a deliberately coarsened sample has equal or better hardness and oxidation resistance than the ultrafine-grained sample, the proposed grain-boundary-based enhancement mechanism is falsified.

contradictions.description: The intervention and conditions include processing up to 1800°C, while the boundary says processing must not exceed the melting point and that temperatures above 1400°C cause detrimental phase formation and grain growth.

The proposed falsification treatment uses SFP above 1400°C even though the stated processing boundary says this range must be avoided; although it may serve as a deliberate negative condition, it is inconsistent with the stated admissible route.
